clue.text: Traditional home of 17 across: note high ground for Guardian when Jethro's about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the musician's possessive name is wrapped round the other pieces

blocks.note: NB, nota bene, is a written note to take heed
a ridge is a stretch of high ground
the Guardian speaking for itself uses the editorial we
Jethro Tull, the agricultural pioneer (and the rock band), so Jethro's is Tull's

explanation.surface: A setter for the Guardian musing on a Kent spa town, a hilltop and the farming innovator Jethro Tull.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 across: 'Disgusted of Tunbridge Wells' is the stock name for an indignant letter-writer to British newspapers; Tunbridge Wells is a genteel town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial angry letter-writer signs off as Disgusted, Tunbridge Wells, so that Kent town is his traditional address.

clue.text: Special offer - offer Co-op were not making

annotation.answer: TWO FOR THE PRICE OF ONE

blocks.note: first meaning: a shop deal giving a second item free
second, jokey meaning: in the word Co-op the hyphen keeps its pair of Os sounding separately, unlike coop where they merge into a single vowel sound

explanation.surface: A bargain promotion that the Co-op supermarket chain declined to run.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a British retail cooperative. Its name is written with a hyphen, so its two Os are said as two vowels, not squeezed into one as in a chicken coop.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal where a buyer pays for a single item and gets a second free is the classic shop promotion of that name.

clue.text: Court accessory that keeps one on line?

definitions.text: Court accessory that keeps one on line?

blocks.note: surface reading: something worn or carried at a royal court
setter's reading: a tennis court fitting, the cable along the top that holds the barrier taut in a straight line

explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests royalty, but it is a tennis court; the item holds the net up in a line across it.
explanation.definitionFit: The cord or cable running along the top of a tennis net, holding it stretched across the court, has that name.

clue.text: Theatrical term for one leaving harvester at a party

indicators.note: the letter for one walks out of the machine's name, so it is dropped

blocks.note: A is the indefinite article, meaning one
a reaper is a harvesting machine or worker
the Tory party, Britain's Conservatives

explanation.surface: Someone at a party slips away from a farm worker, and a stage word is wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A out of REAPER to leave REPER, then add TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Repertory is the theatre word for a company performing a stock of plays in rotation, or that stock itself.

clue.text: Deuterium is reportedly not allowed to break up

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the phrase for forbidden is taken by its sound

blocks.note: D is the chemical symbol for deuterium
taken as written
banned means not allowed, and is said like band

explanation.surface: A chemistry claim that heavy hydrogen is forbidden from splitting apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To disband is to dissolve a group, so its members break up and go separate ways.

clue.text: Previous partner wasn't good-looking - that will be the reason

definitions.note: a phrase, as in 'that will explain it'

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
plain means not attractive

explanation.surface: Someone decides a former partner's lack of looks accounts for the breakup.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: something that will be the reason is something that will account for, or clarify, what happened.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to give its cause, and a cause is a reason, so a fact that does so serves to clarify events.

clue.text: English lake causing feelings of discomfort

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Lake Erie, one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: An English lake that makes visitors uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncanny and strange makes people uneasy, giving them unsettled, creepy sensations.

clue.text: Stopped, left alone and given the sack

blocks.note: first meaning: ceased doing something, as in laying off the drink
second meaning: stopped bothering someone, as in 'lay off him'
third meaning: dismissed from a job

explanation.surface: A worker halted, abandoned and fired all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one phrasal verb, not two.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers quitting a habit, ceasing to pester somebody, and an employer dismissing staff when work runs short.

clue.text: Score with dessert - hence I ask kiss

blocks.note: a sweet is a dessert in British usage
with means together with, joined by and
a score is twenty

explanation.surface: A diner pairs a tally with a pudding and then asks for a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in reverse order in the clue. The definition quotes Feste's song in Twelfth Night: 'Then come kiss me, sweet and twenty'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's song the singer begs a kiss of his young darling because she is so lovely, so the phrase is the ground for asking.

clue.text: A month's work on the bed

blocks.note: OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October
an opus is a work, especially a musical one

explanation.surface: Someone spends a whole month working while lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests a bedroom, but it is the sea bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The eight-armed cephalopod lives on the seafloor, so it is found down there among the rocks.

clue.text: Scope for simple direction about 6

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for simple wraps round the Roman number

blocks.note: pure means simple, unmixed
VI is six in Roman numerals
W for west, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A plain instruction concerning item six sets the range of a task.
explanation.walkthrough: PUR(VI)E then W; the 6 is the number itself, not a reference to 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A purview is the range of a person's authority or concern, which is its extent or reach.

clue.text: Guardian's holding a party, which goes up one's nose

indicators.note: holding means gripping inside, so the possessive word encloses the party

blocks.note: the Guardian speaking of itself says our, the editorial possessive
a do is a party

explanation.surface: The newspaper throws a party that irritates somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: O(DO)UR. 'Goes up one's nose' sounds like the idiom for annoying someone, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell is something drawn in through the nostrils, so it literally rises into the nasal passages.

clue.text: Silver for primate - a lot of money - of dubious sect

indicators.note: a lot of is most but not all, so the final letter of the cash word is cut

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
an ape is a primate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shady cult charging a monkey's weight in silver and a fortune besides.
explanation.walkthrough: The Agapemone, or Abode of Love, was a notorious Victorian religious community in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agapemonites were a scandal-ridden nineteenth-century English religious community, a disreputable cult.

clue.text: Edward and Dorothy keep memory coming back where the Roses meet

indicators.note: the couple keep something between them, holding it inside
coming back means the whole string is read from right to left

blocks.note: Ned is a pet form of Edward
ROM, read-only memory in a computer
Dot is a pet form of Dorothy

explanation.surface: A couple cherish a recollection of the place where two flowers grow together.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roses are Lancashire (red) and Yorkshire (white), after the Wars of the Roses; Todmorden is a town straddling their old county boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pennine town historically sat across the Lancashire and Yorkshire border, so the two rival counties join there.

clue.text: Capital one in seat for more

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the furniture word

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a sofa is a seat for more than one person

explanation.surface: A capital city where one person sits on a seat built for several.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of Bulgaria, a national capital in the Balkans.

clue.text: Slight crushing sound holds the West up, being easily 17 across

indicators.note: holds means grips inside, so the crushing noise encloses the actress
in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: a squish is a soft squelching crunch
Mae West, the film star, the West of Hollywood fame

explanation.surface: A soft crunching noise is supposed to support the western world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The West' looks like the compass point or the western world; it is the actress Mae West. 17 across means revolted.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeamish person is readily nauseated or repelled, quick to feel revulsion at unpleasant things.

clue.text: Find pleasure in Trollope's "Is he Pop____ ?"

blocks.note: Is He Popenjoy? is a novel by Anthony Trollope; the blank stands for the missing end of the title name

explanation.surface: A reader is invited to delight in a Victorian novel with a quizzical title.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blank to complete the title; the letters that fill it are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something is to take delight or satisfaction from it, which is the same as liking it.

clue.text: A jewel of which the opening may develop an itch ...

indicators.note: the opening is the very start, so only the first letter of the gem word is kept
something that develops grows into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of jewel
the six letters of an itch rearranged

explanation.surface: A gem whose wearer might break out in an itch where it sits.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 17 down, which offers a second jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacinth is a reddish-orange variety of zircon, a precious stone used in jewellery.

clue.text: Far from pleased the south wind ceased to blow outside

indicators.note: outside means lying around the rest, so the word for stopped surrounds the wind

blocks.note: died means stopped, as an engine dies
S is the abbreviation for south
a gust is a burst of wind
surface padding: completes the phrase ceased to blow and gives no letters

explanation.surface: Someone is unhappy that the southerly breeze has stopped blowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ceased to blow' reads as one phrase about the wind, but only 'ceased to' supplies letters, and they wrap round the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone revolted or outraged is feeling the very opposite of happy or satisfied.

clue.text: ...  and one to suit for the weekend I am on duty

definitions.note: continues 16 down: another jewel, and also a suit of cards

indicators.note: for here means standing in for, so the letters spanning the following words serve as the answer

blocks.note: the hidden run starts at the final letter of this word
both words are taken whole
taken whole
the hidden run stops at the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A worker on the weekend rota is rewarded with a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to 16 down: after one jewel, 'and one' is another jewel, and also a suit of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is a precious gem, and diamonds is also one of the four suits in a pack of cards.

clue.text: Law officer gives a lady a piece of music

blocks.note: she is the pronoun for a lady
a riff is a short repeated musical phrase

explanation.surface: A lawman hands a woman a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheriff is a county official charged with keeping the peace, a lawman in the American West.

clue.text: Agreed with model having friends?

blocks.note: the Model T, Ford's famous car
allied means joined with friends, partners in an alliance

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fashion model who went along with the plan has pals.
explanation.walkthrough: Model suggests a catwalk, but it is the Ford Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: When two accounts tallied they matched up, so one corresponded to and was consistent with the other.

clue.text: Academic post to found in terrace building

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the little word goes within the row of houses
building means constructing something new, so the letters are put together in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A university appointment involves founding something inside a row of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectorate is the office of a rector, the head of some universities and colleges.

clue.text: See 1 down
Let everyone say: "That hurt!"

blocks.note: all means everyone
ow is the cry of pain

explanation.surface: Everybody yells out in pain at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone do something is to permit them, giving them permission.

clue.text: Briskly read a French word that may be good for nothing

blocks.note: to con is to study or read carefully

blocks.clueFragment: a French word that may be good
blocks.note: mot is French for word, and a bon mot is a good one, a witticism
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A study of French vocabulary where a clever word may turn out worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good for nothing' looks like one phrase meaning useless, but 'good' finishes the hint at bon mot and 'nothing' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Con moto is an Italian musical direction meaning with movement, played at a lively pace.

clue.text: Spectral Scotsman following Irish instincts?

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the Scotsman's name is placed last

blocks.note: IR is the abbreviation for Irish
the id is the instinctive part of the mind in Freudian theory
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A ghostly Scot driven by Irish gut feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectral' suggests a ghost, but here it means of the spectrum, like a rainbow.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridian means relating to the iris or rainbow, so it describes colours of the light spectrum.

clue.text: Sunset in the long term?

definitions.note: the answer follows 'at' in this sense: at the end of the day

blocks.note: first meaning: the close of daylight, evening
second meaning: the idiom 'at ...', ultimately

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second meaning needs the preposition at in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk literally closes the daylight hours, and the cliché means when all is considered, eventually.
